classification.difficultyReason: Infer two height-difference equations from paired arrangements and eliminate both people's heights.

content.prompt: How tall is the box shown below?

spec.description: Two paired arrangements with aligned ground levels: female on a box and male on the ground at left; male on an identical box and female on the ground at right. Repeated figures have identical heights. Unfilled red and blue outlines distinguish the two people; decorative source fills are omitted.
spec.mathematics: The left head-height difference is 1.4 m and the right head-height difference is 2.1 m. Both double-ended arrows terminate at dashed guides through the respective head tops. Drawing coordinates specify illustrative proportions only, not additional numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied differences are visible; no box height or person height is supplied.

inlines.text: Add the two height differences to obtain twice the box height.

answer.worked:
Let $h$, $f$ and $m$ be the heights in metres of the box, female and male respectively.
$$\begin{align*}
h+f-m&=1.4\\
h+m-f&=2.1
\end{align*}$$
Adding the equations eliminates both people's heights:
$$\begin{align*}
2h&=3.5\\
h&=1.75
\end{align*}$$
The box is $1.75\,\mathrm{m}$ tall.
